title: 3797. Count Routes to Climb a Rectangular Grid

examples.explanation: We label the cells we visit in the routes sequentially, starting from 1. The two routes are: .2 #1 32 #1 We can move from the cell (1, 1) to the cell (0, 1) because the Euclidean distance is sqrt((1 - 0)2 + (1 - 1)2) = sqrt(1) <= d. However, we cannot move from the cell (1, 1) to the cell (0, 0) because the Euclidean distance is sqrt((1 - 0)2 + (1 - 0)2) = sqrt(2) > d.
Two of the routes are given in example 1. The other two routes are: 2. #1 23 #1 Note that we can move from (1, 1) to (0, 0) because the Euclidean distance is sqrt(2) <= d.
We cannot choose any cell as the starting cell. Therefore, there are no routes.
